name: AD — Kerberoasting: RC4 Service Ticket Requested
description:
Attacker objective
Request RC4 (0x17) Kerberos service tickets for SPN-bearing accounts to crack their passwords offline (Kerberoasting).

Attack logic
In an AES-enforced domain, RC4 service tickets are rare and belong to a few legacy accounts. An RC4 service-ticket request for any other account is an encryption downgrade characteristic of Kerberoasting tooling.

Why this detection works
Event 4769 records the ticket encryption type and the target service, so allowlisting known legacy RC4 accounts turns any other 0x17 service ticket into a high-signal event.

False positives
Additional legacy RC4-only service accounts.

Tuning
Add verified legacy accounts to the exclusion; investigate any RC4 request for a modern account.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 4769 (TicketEncryptionType, ServiceName, TargetUserName).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. TargetUserName = the requesting account; ServiceName = the SPN targeted.
2. An RC4 downgrade for a non-legacy service is Kerberoasting; reset the SPN account password (long/complex) and hunt for offline cracking follow-on.
query: event.code:"4769" and winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType:"0x17" and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName:"rpap" and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName:"krbtgt"
